paper_metadata.title: Reduction of Qubits in Quantum Algorithm for Monte Carlo Simulation by Pseudo-random Number Generator

experiments.description: Theoretical quantum Monte Carlo scheme that replaces parallel random-number registers with a sequential pseudo-random number generator (PCG) on a quantum circuit, combined with amplitude estimation to estimate the average sampled integrand value.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Monte Carlo with sequential PRNG (PCG) and amplitude estimation

hyperparameters.nsamp: number of sample subsequences; examples discussed: 10, 20, 30
hyperparameters.Nran: number of random numbers required per integrand evaluation
hyperparameters.Norac: number of oracle calls for amplitude estimation
hyperparameters.delta: confidence parameter in amplitude estimation (mentioned symbolically)

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Prepare uniform superposition over sample indices with Hadamard gates; PRNG seed and parameters are chosen according to the PRNG used.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Sample index register Rsamp uses nsamp qubits to encode i in superposition; PRN register RPRN stores sequential pseudo-random bit strings; integrand register Rint stores intermediate and final sampled integrand values; phase ancilla Rph encodes the integrand value into amplitude.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate Esamp = arithmetic average of sampled integrand values, as an approximation to the Monte Carlo integral.
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: At least 1 phase ancilla (Rph); additional ancillas may be required by arithmetic subroutines.

problem_instance.description: Generic high-dimensional Monte Carlo integration / financial simulation setting; no single concrete numerical instance beyond the illustrative credit-risk and toy integration examples.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Uniform PRNs are converted to desired distributions inside the integrand calculation (e.g., via Box-Muller for normal variables, assumed implementable as quantum gates).
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical error analysis comparing quantum method, previous quantum Monte Carlo, and classical Monte Carlo; no physical hardware benchmark.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: nsamp + nPRN + nint + 1, plus any ancillas required by subroutines
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: Dominated by sequential PRNG progression; scales with Nran and modular multiplication depth O(n^2) for PCG background LCG

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: None beyond choosing PRNG parameters and sample size; theoretical discussion only.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Amplitude estimation on the phase ancilla to recover the average sampled integrand value.

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming amplitude estimation is used and the sampled-integrand expectation Esamp is estimated with oracle calls Norac = O(1/epsilon)
speedup_claims.caveats: There is a trade-off: qubit reduction via sequential PRNG increases circuit depth, which scales with Nran; full reduction may be impractical on near-term hardware.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Error scales as O(Nsamp^-1/2 + Norac^-1); with target error epsilon, Norac = O(1/epsilon) and Nsamp = O(1/epsilon^2)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/epsilon^2) oracle calls for classical Monte Carlo
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: 2πd sqrt(Esamp(1-Esamp)) in the amplitude-estimation error term
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_classical: c sigma_fNran in the classical sampling error term

experiments.description: Theoretical application of the sequential-PRNG quantum Monte Carlo method to credit risk measurement under the Merton model, computing portfolio loss and enabling VaR/CVaR estimation.

algorithm.variant: Quantum credit-risk Monte Carlo with sequential PRNG (PCG) under the Merton model
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Generate a standard normal systematic factor in register Rcom; initialize loss register RL to 0; initialize PRN subsequences via JPRN.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One PRN value per obligor is processed sequentially; loss register RL accumulates exposures Ei when xi < Yi(epsilon_com).
problem_formulation.objective_function: L = sum_i Ei * 1[Zi < zi], with Zi = alpha_i * epsilon_com + sqrt(1 - alpha_i^2) * epsilon_i.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator and controlled adder implement the indicator function and conditional accumulation of loss.
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: At least one comparator ancilla plus ancillas for arithmetic and normal-distribution preparation

problem_instance.description: Generic credit portfolio loss under the Merton model; no specific portfolio size or obligor data are instantiated numerically in the paper.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Systematic factor epsilon_com is precomputed/loaded; conditional default probabilities Pi(epsilon_com) are computed from model parameters; PRNs are used as idiosyncratic factors.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Circuit-level conceptual design only; no numerical benchmark or hardware run reported for the credit-risk case.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: nsamp + nPRN + ncom + nL + comparator/adder ancillas
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: Sequential over Nobl obligors; dominated by repeated PRNG progression and per-obligor comparison/addition

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute conditional default probabilities Pi(epsilon_com) and thresholds zi from model parameters.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Use amplitude estimation on the loss-encoding ancilla/register to estimate loss distribution statistics such as VaR and CVaR.

speedup_claims.conditions: for estimating portfolio loss statistics under the Merton model using amplitude estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: No numerical benchmark or hardware run is reported for the credit-risk case; the result is a circuit-level conceptual design.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Theoretical quadratic speedup in sampling error; overall oracle complexity O(1/epsilon) for amplitude estimation plus sequential per-obligor processing
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical Monte Carlo loss estimation scales as O(1/epsilon^2) samples

experiments.description: Simulator demonstration of the sequential-PRNG quantum Monte Carlo method on a two-variable trigonometric integral, using Qiskit and amplitude estimation without phase estimation.

algorithm.variant: Amplitude estimation without phase estimation applied to PRNG-based Monte Carlo integration
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initialize all registers to |0>; use LCG seed 1; prepare sample superposition with Hadamards; use Qiskit simulator.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two PRN values x_j are mapped to grid points (x_j + 1/2)/2^r and accumulated into the phase of a single ancilla via controlled Ry rotations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: I = (1/theta^Nvar) * integral_0^theta dx1 ... integral_0^theta dxNvar sin^2(sum_i xi).

problem_instance.description: Toy two-dimensional integral used as a proof-of-concept for the PRNG-based quantum Monte Carlo method.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discrete approximation of the integral using PRN-generated grid points; PRN sequence generated by LCG with parameters a=11, c=0, m=31 and seed 1.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared exact integral value, exact average over sampled points, and quantum-simulator estimate; amplitude estimation uses M=8, Nk=100, mk=2^k.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: nsamp + nPRN + 1, plus any ancillas required by arithmetic/control in the PRNG and amplitude-estimation subroutines
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: Not explicitly reported; includes sequential PRNG updates and controlled Ry rotations

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute the PRN sequence and discretized sample points; set up the likelihood function for amplitude estimation without phase estimation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Maximum-likelihood estimation over theta_a from repeated measurements of the ancilla across Grover powers mk.

reported_values.quantity: exact average of integrand values on sample points
estimate by the method in Section V

classical_baselines.method_name: exact average of integrand values on sample points

speedup_claims.conditions: proof-of-concept simulator demonstration only; no runtime comparison is reported
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper demonstrates numerical agreement of the quantum-simulator estimate with the exact average over sampled points, not a speedup benchmark.
